title: Willey wouldn't stop struggling, inquest told
article: Two police officers who said they tasered Clayton Alvin Willey July 21, 2003, testified in the coroner's inquest into his death Friday.

Under questioning from lawyer Dan Weatherly, Prince George Const. Glen Caston said he used the taser on Willey's upper arm for about five seconds after he had been brought in to the RCMP detachment building late in the afternoon of July 21. Const. Kevin O'Donnell said he tasered Willey at almost exactly the same time in the upper left back area.
Willey, 33, died in hospital July 22, 2003, about 16 hours after he was initially arrested in the parking lot of Parkwood Place mall by Prince George RCMP for allegedly causing a disturbance.
He was hog-tied and handcuffed, but still struggling against police, at the time he was tasered, inquest participants heard.

Caston said, "I was concerned he could hurt himself thrashing about on the floor. We needed to control his head-banging on the cement. We were concerned he would continue to try to hurt himself if we didn't intervene."
O'Donnell said, "I have never seen anything like the strength that he had. He was straightening his legs out in the hog-tie.
"There was concern that he was going to break out of the hog- tie," O'Donnell said.

Weatherly asked O'Donnell if he had reported to a staff sergeant on duty that Willey had been tasered three times between his arrest and the arrival of an ambulance to take him to hospital shortly after 5:30 p.m. on July 21, 2003. "It's possible -- three times," O'Donnell replied.
"The idea of calling an ambulance to assist in controlling Mr. Willey was to have him sedated?" Weatherly asked.
Weatherly asked questions about how Willey had been removed from a police Suburban van on being brought into the RCMP vehicle bay and the taken to an elevator up to the booking area and cells.
O'Donnell said he had been assisting Caston in removing Willey from the vehicle.
Weatherly asked if no one was supporting Willey's upper torso as he was being taken out of the vehicle. O'Donnell said no.

His head glanced off the door frame of the van, the inquest heard. "Was he dragged face down?" Weatherly inquired. O'Donnell said yes. "Why was there no support in a more gentle way?" Weatherly asked. O'Donnell said there was no explanation.
Const. Jana Scott, formerly of the Prince George RCMP but now with the Salmon Arm detachment, testified by speaker phone.

She said Willey was still kicking his legs and struggling when brought into the booking area. Officers were asking him to calm down, she said. She said the use of the tasers had had no effect. "I was shocked that it didn't do anything," Scott said. "He kept kicking and struggling."
Soon afterwards, however, Willey stopped struggling, and Scott observed a grayish colour come over his body.
The inquest continues Monday at 9 a.m. in the Plaza 400 building.
